title: CNN Basics — Slide One Detector Across the Picture
key_insight: A convolution slides one small filter across the image. The same filter looks for the same pattern wherever it appears.
body:
## Slide One Detector Across the Picture

An edge can appear in the top-left or bottom-right of an image. Learning a separate detector for every location wastes effort.

A convolution slides one small filter across the image. The same filter looks for the same pattern wherever it appears.

Different filters learn different patterns. Early layers may find edges; later layers combine them into textures, parts, and objects.
common_mistakes: A CNN requires a separate full model for every pixel.
Stride means the number of class labels.
Padding always deletes the image border.
mini_exercise: Sketch the situation in “Slide One Detector Across the Picture” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: CNNs exploit image structure, using fewer parameters than connecting every pixel to every output.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Slide One Detector Across the Picture” situation, explain CNN Basics without assuming the listener knows deep learning.
